findings.claim: In August 2020 Interactive Brokers paid $38 million in penalties to the SEC, FINRA and the CFTC over anti-money-laundering failures, including not filing more than 150 suspicious activity reports on potentially manipulative microcap trades. It settled without admitting or denying the SEC's findings; no individual was charged.

In July 2025 Interactive Brokers paid OFAC $11.8 million over 12,367 apparent sanctions violations from 2016 to 2024, including services to customers located in Iran, Cuba, Syria and Crimea and transfers to blocked Russian banks. OFAC found them non-egregious and voluntarily self-disclosed; the company says the matter is concluded.

A 2015 customer class action alleged flaws in the automated system Interactive Brokers uses to liquidate margin-deficient accounts; a class was certified in 2023. A settlement approved in June 2026 paid the class $5 million and forgave about $1.8 million of customer debts, with no admission of liability.

Press reports based on federal campaign filings say Peterffy gave $2.8 million to Keystone Renewal, the super PAC backing Dave McCormick's 2024 Pennsylvania Senate bid, and $1.5 million in July-September 2024 to Maryland's Future, a pro-Hogan super PAC. NBC News reported two $1 million gifts from him to Virginia Governor Youngkin's PAC in 2023.

Interactive Brokers' 2025 annual report says Peterffy and his affiliates hold about 91.6% of the economic interests and all voting interests in the holding company that carries about 73.7% of the group's voting power, so he can elect the whole board. The company is a Nasdaq controlled company, and Peterffy chairs its compensation committee.

Social 1 to 2: the rubric names consumer settlements at level 2; the $5M settlement is modest, so 1 is defensible. Unresolved stays 0. No disbursed giving by Peterffy himself was found.
